h1: The 7 Best Mouse Pads for Wireless Charging of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Mouse Pads for Wireless Charging: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 wireless charging mouse pads scored on charging output, safety protection, extra coils, surface and lighting.
summary: The 4-in-1 Wireless Charging Mouse Pad with Foldable Phone Holder is the best of the group, charging a phone and earbuds together at 15W. The TARKARI is the budget standout, with six listed safety protections and a woven surface. The RGB model with a phone stand is the one for desks that want a propped screen. The Logitech G POWERPLAY 2 is a different kind of product and deserves a careful read before buying.
intro: The headline spec on most wireless charging mouse pads is 15W, and it is nearly always a ceiling, not a promise. Charging speed depends on the phone, the case thickness and how well the coil lines up with your device. Put a phone on the wrong spot and a 15W pad will deliver far less, or nothing at all.

So we ranked these seven pads by what a real desk needs: a stated charging output, safety protections for a surface that sits under your hand all day, extra coils or stands and a mouse surface that does not fight the cable you also have to hide. We reviewed the listings, not retail hype, and scored each on the Primea framework.

products.name: Wireless Charging Mouse Pad with Foldable Phone Holder
products.verdict: A 4-in-1 desk mat that charges a phone and AirPods together at 15W.
products.description:
This 4-in-1 desk mat lists 15W fast wireless charging and says you can charge a phone and AirPods at the same time. The combination matters because most single-coil pads force a choice, while a desk mat with a second charging area keeps your earbuds topped up without another cable.

It wins because the other pads here either charge one device or hide the details. Against the RGB model with a phone stand it adds the foldable holder and a second charging spot, and it sits in the top price bucket of $50 to $100.

It suits a one-desk, many-gadget setup. Expect to learn where each coil sits, since misaligned devices charge slowly or not at all.
products.idealFor: Desk users who charge a phone and earbuds side by side.
products.skipIf: You only need a basic mouse pad with a single coil.

products.name: TARKARI Mouse Pad Gaming Wireless Charging
products.verdict: 15W multi-level charging with six safety protections for under $25.
products.description:
TARKARI's listing is unusually specific: 15W multi-level fast wireless charging with six safety protections, ten RGB light modes with an inductive touch switch and a high-density woven fabric surface. Safety protections matter on a charger you rest a warm phone on, because over-heat and foreign-object cutoffs are what separate a good pad from a fire risk.

It ranks second because it lacks the second charging area of the top pick, and the touch switch for lighting is a feature you may or may not want. It also costs under $25, the lowest bucket in the group.

A smart choice for gamers who want a clean surface and honest safety specs. Skip it if you need earbuds charging too.
products.idealFor: Gamers wanting a safe, well-specified pad for little money.
products.skipIf: You also want earbuds or a second device charged.

products.name: Wireless Charging RGB Mouse Pad with Phone Stand
products.verdict: A dual-charging desk mat with a foldable stand and adjustable RGB lighting.
products.description:
This model is a dual wireless charging desk mat with a foldable phone stand and adjustable RGB lighting. A propped phone at eye level means you read notifications without moving your hand off the mouse, and a stand also keeps the phone aligned on its coil.

Its listing leaves out a wattage figure, unlike the 15W pads above it, so charging speed cannot be compared. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket, which makes it cheaper than the top pick, though without the AirPods spot.

Buy it for a desk where the phone should stay upright and visible. Skip it if you want documented charging output.
cons: Stand adds bulk to the desk
products.idealFor: Desk users who want the phone propped at eye level.
products.skipIf: You want a stated charging speed.

products.name: 15W Wireless Charging Mouse Pad with Wrist Support
products.verdict: A 15W Qi charger with a wrist rest, for people who type and click all day.
products.description:
This is a 15W Qi wireless charger built into a mouse pad with an ergonomic wrist support and multiple protection features. A wrist rest cushions the heel of your hand against the desk edge, which is the comfort feature other pads here skip.

It ranks fourth because the listing gives few details on the protections or surface, and the wrist support is a different priority from the extra coils and stands above. It is the better pick over the plain 15W model below if comfort matters, and it sits under $25.

A fit for office workers on long shifts. Skip it if you want RGB lighting or a stand, since none is listed.
products.idealFor: Office users who want comfort and a built-in charger.
products.skipIf: You want RGB lighting or a propped phone.

products.name: Wireless Charging Mouse Pad
products.verdict: A 15W charging pad with 16 lighting modes and a 4mm thick surface.
products.description:
This pad lists 15W fast charge, 11 plus 5 dynamic lighting modes and a 4mm thick build. The thickness matters because a thin pad lets the charging coil and cable ridges show through under the mouse, while 4mm smooths them out.

It ranks fifth because the listing offers no safety protections or stand and the name is generic, so you have less to verify than on the TARKARI. It stays under $25, so it undercuts the stand and wrist models above.

Choose it for a straightforward, well-lit pad on a small budget. Skip it if you want earbuds charging or a documented list of protections.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want a lit, thick pad.
products.skipIf: You need a stand or documented protections.

products.name: XXL Mouse Pad with Phone Holder
products.verdict: An oversized desk pad with fast charging, a phone holder and 11 RGB modes.
products.description:
The XXL pad is an oversized desk mat with fast charging, a phone holder and 11 RGB lighting modes. An oversize mat gives room for keyboard and mouse, so you can sweep the mouse without it falling off the edge.

It ranks sixth because the listing does not state a wattage or safety protections, which makes the charging claim vague. At $25 to $50 it costs more than the TARKARI and gives you less to verify. The holder keeps the phone visible, a plus over the plain pads.

Buy it if desk coverage is the priority. Skip it if you need to know how fast it charges.
products.idealFor: Users who want full desk coverage with a phone holder.
products.skipIf: You need a documented charging speed.

products.name: Logitech G POWERPLAY 2 Wireless Charging Mouse Pad
products.verdict: A branded pad built around non-stop wireless charging, not phone charging.
products.description:
Logitech's listing promises non-stop wireless charging, plug, power, play and a future-ready wireless system, with no wattage and no phone-charging claim. That wording points to a different job from the other pads: the pad is meant to keep a compatible wireless gaming mouse powered while you play.

It ranks last because the listing gives you no way to compare it on phone charging, which is what most buyers want, and it costs $50 to $100, the same bucket as the top pick. It is the one to consider only if you already own a compatible Logitech mouse.

Skip it if you want to charge a phone or earbuds, and check the product page for mouse compatibility first.
products.idealFor: Owners of a compatible Logitech gaming mouse.
products.skipIf: You want to charge a phone or earbuds.

methodology.title: Charging output
methodology.description: Pads with a stated wattage scored above those that only claim fast charging, since speed is the whole point of the product.

methodology.title: Safety protections
methodology.description: Listed over-heat and foreign-object protections were credited because the charger sits under your hand and next to a warm phone.

methodology.title: Charging coverage
methodology.description: We weighed second charging areas, stands and holders against single-coil pads.

methodology.title: Mouse surface
methodology.description: Thickness, fabric and size were judged for tracking comfort and for how well the pad hides the coil underneath.

methodology.title: Lighting and extras
methodology.description: RGB modes, wrist supports and touch switches were treated as extras, not a substitute for charging quality.

whatMatters.detail: A wattage figure such as 15W tells you the best-case charging speed. Real speeds depend on your phone, its case and how well it sits on the coil. Look for a number in the listing, and treat a pad with only the words fast charging as unproven rather than slow.

A wireless charger sits under a warm phone, so over-temperature, over-current and foreign-object protections matter. The TARKARI lists six. Search the listing for those protections by name and prefer pads that name them. A vague line about multiple protection is better than nothing, but it is not something you can check.

Wireless charging only works when the phone sits near the coil, so a pad with a marked charging zone or a stand makes life easier. A phone placed slightly off will charge slowly or stop. Check for a marked area in the listing's photos, and keep thick cases or metal plates off the coil.

A thicker surface hides the coil and keeps mouse tracking smooth, while a thin one may let the charger show through. The 4mm build on one listing is an example. Check thickness in the specifications, and look for stitched edges or a non-slip base so the pad stays put.

A USB cable runs from the pad to a wall adapter, and a short cord limits where you can put it. An oversized pad needs a deep desk. Measure your desk, check the cable length and the adapter requirement in the listing, since many pads do not include a wall plug.

faq.q: Will these pads charge any phone?
faq.a: They charge phones that support Qi wireless charging, such as those on the 15W Wireless Charging Mouse Pad with Wrist Support. A thick case or metal plate can block charging. Check your phone's wireless charging support before buying any of them.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with charging mouse pads?
faq.a: Placing the phone off-centre. The coil is smaller than the pad, so a phone parked on the TARKARI or the generic Wireless Charging Mouse Pad may charge slowly or not at all. Find the charging zone and mark it.

faq.q: Is the foldable holder desk mat worth it over the TARKARI?
faq.a: Only if you charge more than one device. The 4-in-1 mat charges a phone and AirPods together at 15W, while the TARKARI charges one device for under $25 and lists six protections. For a single phone, the TARKARI is enough.

faq.q: How do I set up a wireless charging mouse pad?
faq.a: Plug the USB cable into a wall adapter, since many pads ship without one, then place the pad where the cord reaches. Put your phone on the charging area. On the RGB model with a phone stand, unfold the holder first.

faq.q: How do I maintain the surface?
faq.a: Wipe the cloth surface with a damp cloth and let it dry fully before powering the pad. Keep liquids away from the USB port, and unplug it before cleaning the XXL Mouse Pad with Phone Holder or any other RGB model.

faq.q: Does the Logitech POWERPLAY 2 charge a phone?
faq.a: Its listing does not say so. The Logitech G POWERPLAY 2 is described around non-stop wireless charging and plug, power, play, with no phone claim or wattage. Treat it as a mouse-charging product, and confirm compatibility on the product page.

finalTake: The Wireless Charging Mouse Pad with Foldable Phone Holder is the best choice if you charge more than a phone, thanks to its 15W output and AirPods spot. The TARKARI is the budget answer, with six listed protections for under $25. The RGB model with a phone stand suits propped screens, and the wrist-support pad suits long typing days. Treat the Logitech G POWERPLAY 2 as a specialist product, and read its compatibility before buying.
